title: Theatre Seat Reservations
instructions:
Implement `SeatMap` and the two helpers in `seats.py`. A theatre has rows A through Z
(at most 26), with seats numbered 1 through seats_per_row. All ordered seat lists use
row order then numeric seat order, so A2 comes before A10.

- `seat_label(row: int, number: int) -> str` uses a zero-based row index and one-based
  seat number. Require integer (not bool) row in 0..25 and positive integer (not bool)
  number; otherwise `ValueError`.
- `parse_seat(label: str, rows: int, seats_per_row: int) -> tuple[int, int]` returns
  (zero-based row, one-based number). Require exact uppercase labels such as A1 or B12;
  no whitespace, leading zeroes, signs or extra characters. Malformed/out-of-bounds labels
  raise `ValueError`. Its dimension arguments are assumed valid.
- `SeatMap(rows: int, seats_per_row: int)` requires integer, non-bool dimensions, rows
  1..26 and seats_per_row >= 1; invalid dimensions raise `ValueError`.
- `reserve(labels, owner: str) -> list[str]`: labels is an iterable of strings. Owner must
  be a nonempty string (whitespace is allowed), otherwise `ValueError`. Validate all labels,
  deduplicate, then reserve them atomically. Any already occupied seat, even by the same
  owner, raises `ValueError`; any error leaves the map unchanged. Return reserved labels
  in seat order. An empty iterable returns [].
- `release(owner: str) -> list[str]` frees every seat held by that exact owner and returns
  sorted labels; unknown owners return [].
- `available(row: str) -> list[str]` returns free labels for an exact one-letter uppercase
  row. Invalid or out-of-bounds rows raise `ValueError`.
- `reserve_block(row: str, size: int, owner: str) -> list[str] | None` reserves the leftmost
  run of size free adjacent seats in that row. Validate row, positive integer non-bool size,
  and owner even if no block fits. Invalid inputs raise `ValueError`; no fitting block returns
  None without mutation. A size greater than the row width is valid but cannot fit.
- `snapshot() -> dict[str, str]` maps occupied labels to owners in seat order; it is a copy.

## Files
- `seats.py`
